input.question: How reliable are deep research agents when the evidence they find is misleading or incomplete?

supporting.quote: introducing one misleading document increases the mean FCAR from 0% in the no-injection control to 54.7%
supporting.why: One misleading document leads to false conclusions in 54.7% of reports.

supporting.quote: they may commit to claims before sufficient evidence is available, causing later reasoning to reinforce an incorrect interpretation
supporting.why: Agents commit prematurely to wrong claims.

supporting.quote: existing evaluation paradigms predominantly focus on final task outcomes, leaving a significant gap in understanding the intermediate execution traces

draft_answer: Not very: one misleading document pushed mean false-conclusion adoption from 0% to 54.7%, agents commit to claims too early, and outcome-only evaluation hides errors in intermediate steps.
